title: HiPerConTracer dissector + heuristics for decoding ICMP/ICMPv6 payload
description: This MR adds a HiPerConTracer dissector as well as heuristics for decoding ICMP/ICMPv6 payload (i.e. the data sent e.g. with ICMP Echo Request/Reply). HiPerConTracer (https://www.uni-due.de/~be0001/hipercontracer/) is a tool for larger-scale Traceroute and Ping runs, using ICMP Echo Request/Reply messages for obtaining information about RTTs and routes.

Given that the heuristic is not very narrow, maybe it would be better to have it off by default? Fortunately it seems like it does not kick in with a default ICMP request for Linux or Windows.

The heuristic should be okay for most cases. Then, Wireshark can identify HiPerConTracer traffic out of the box, and the user could disable HiPerConTracer completely if this should really lead to false positives. If there is really an example for a false positive, it would also be possible to narrow down the 64-bit time stamp range inside the heuristic.
should the data dissector be called for the data not consumed by the heuristic dissector? This is not the case for your example, but it could be for another one

It should be fine to assume that a sub-dissector can completely dissect the message. There should be no need to try to dissect any more data. The only content for HiPerConTracer ICMP Echo Request/Echo Reply messages is the HiPerConTracer message. This should also be the case for any possible future dissector of other tools based on ICMP Echo Request/Echo Reply.
See my comment above (here offset might not be incremented enough depending on the sub dissector called)
